_meta.question: Should small related memories be consolidated into bigger ones? (synthesis, not dedup)

embedding_facts.history: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384) -> modernbert-embed-base (768). There was never a 785 or a 1024.

_meta.note: Aggregates only; queries derive from verbatim production content.

headroom.reading: Merging 2-3 typical memories stays inside the window. Merging 5 puts nearly half of them past it, and everything past 512 tokens is simply not embedded.

also_measured.note: 0.90 yielded only 7 groups / 15 probes and is not readable. 0.75 folds more aggressively for a larger loss.

honest_limits.first_cut_was_one_sided: The initial harness only built queries from tokens unique to ONE member — the hardest case for a merge. It measured cost and could not see benefit, and it read as a flat 'merging hurts'. The cross-cutting arm was added after noticing that.
honest_limits.part_of_the_benefit_is_structural: before_both requires TWO memories in the top-10; after requires ONE. Some of the 26->77 gain is simply that one item is easier to place than two. That is a real retrieval advantage, not an artifact, but it is not evidence that the merged text is better written.
honest_limits.no_dedup_gain: This is orthogonal to duplication. The store has 0 exact duplicates and 30 value-identical pairs in 5972 memories; merging here folds DISTINCT facts together on purpose.

verdict.answer: Yes, but narrowly: at cosine 0.80, in groups of 2-3, with mmr_union.
verdict.why: At 0.80 the cost is MRR -0.003 and one fact of 169 falling out of the top-10, while cross-cutting queries answered by a single hit go from 26/80 to 77/80. At 0.85 the cost triples (-0.026, 4 facts) for a smaller relative gain.
verdict.do_not: Do not merge more than 3 at a time (5x puts 48% of memories past the 512-token window, where the tail stops being embedded), and do not reuse the dedup path for it — the value guard exists precisely to stop consolidate() from folding diverging facts, which is what this does deliberately.
verdict.not_shipped: Measured, not built. It needs a separate entry point from consolidate(), and the injection-budget effect of larger memories is unmeasured.
